senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to bend, decline from the right path,] to be insincere, to flatter; to show favor in court; to deceive.
units: <cite ref="Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:8">Der. Er. Zuta ch. II</cite> <he>אֶחְנוֹף לזה וכ׳</he> I will flatter (lower myself before) this one that he may give me to eat &c.
<cite ref="Sotah 41b:6">Sot. 41ᵇ</cite> <he>הִחְנִיפוּ לו וכ׳</he> thy flattered Agrippa (saying to him, ‘Thou art our brother’).
<cite ref="Sotah 41b:8">Ib.</cite> <he>מותר להַחְנִיף וכ׳</he> it is permissible to flatter (submit to the power of) the wicked &c. Y. Ber. VII, 11ᶜ.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 25:1">Pesik. R. s. 25</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 24:5">Is. XXIV, 5</cite>) <he>הבריות מַהֲנִיפִים זה לזה</he> men deal insincerely with one another; <he>והוא מַחֲנִיפוֹ וכ׳</he> and he puts him (the priest or Levite) off with deceptive intent, and says &c.; a. fr.
